For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=-\frac{\pi }{6}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)\cdot p(t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,p(t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6}) & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{3})p(-\frac{\pi }{6})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{3}){p}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}\,i+\sqrt{3}\,k)+\frac{1}{2}(-2\,i-8\,j+4\,k) \\  & =(3\,i+3\,k)+(-\,i-4\,j+2\,k) \\  & =2\,i-4\,j+5\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6}):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6})‖ & =\sqrt{(2)^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(5)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{45} \\  & =3\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6}):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(-\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6})}{‖{r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6})‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{5}}\cdot (2\,i-4\,j+5\,k) \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{15}\,i-\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{15}\,j+\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=-\frac{\pi }{6}$ is
 $T(-\frac{\pi }{6})=\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{15}\,i-\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{15}\,j+\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\,k.$
